prerequisites: Minimum knowledge of English is recommended for using software and understanding some readings.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of industrial engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to organize and plan within a company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a team.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework. Business organization and management.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. Understand the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Utilize digital simulation techniques as a tool for analyzing production and logistics systems.
Apply discrete-event oriented system modeling methods.
Use and understand some of the most widely used simulation programs in both research and business.

syllabus_topics: Continuous, discrete, and discrete-event oriented systems.
Statistical simulation models. The Monte Carlo method.
Problem solving using simulation as an analysis tool. Validation of simulation models.
Construction of simulation models of production and/or logistics systems. Analysis of the bottleneck of a production line. Resource optimization.

assessment_methods.method: Punctual Control (CP1) - Written test on theoretical part (manual Monte Carlo simulation)
Punctual Control (CP2) - Practical test (construction and validation of a simple simulation model with Arena)
Individual Tasks (TI) - Resolution of exercises using simulation with Excel and Arena
Final Individual Project (TIF) - Resolution of two cases using simulation, including documentation and public presentation

assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, the sum of CP1+CP2+TI must be at least 1 point. The Final Individual Project (TIF) must have a minimum score of 2 points. If all minimums are reached, the final grade is calculated as NOTA = CP1 + CP2 + TI + TIF. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated formula and 4.0. For the extraordinary examination, CP1 and CP2 scores are kept; a new opportunity is offered for TI, and TIF must be presented. Differentiated evaluation requires students to submit the same individual/group assignments and present the final individual project.
